title: Winning the battle of bands over Moten and Andy Kirk
summary: Goodwin and Lovett recall the band entering in uniform, winning the crowd, and beating Moten's band, Andy Kirk and others.

bands.name: Andy Kirk and His Clouds of Joy

story.theme_name: Who was in the band: naming sidemen and personnel

blocks.x: You remember that, Baby?
Sure.
You were in that tan suit, weren't you?
Sure, man.
And then when we did get -- I think we was about the fifth or sixth band to play. When we got on that stand it was pandemonium.
You really broke it up?
We played about three tunes and it just broke the house down. The roof caved in and I'm telling you --
Who was some of the leading competition?
There was Benny Moten.
Benny Moten. That was his rejects beating him out?
That's right.
That's one of the reasons they played so well I'll bet, to show Benny what he lost, huh?
Actually I think the rejects played over their heads, really, because the band did sound good.
Who else? There was Moten's band and two or three or one or two of the other leading bands that were competing with you.
Andy Kirk.
Andy Kirk.

Andy Kirk. All the big name bands. It was a band here by the name of Paul Banks. He was there. Well, he had a band out of -- down the road here in Missouri -- Sedalia -- Sedalia Night Hawks, they had about an eight piece band. It was a good little band but --
How about Jay McShann, was he there?
Jay McShann was doing singles then. He
hadn't come up. Jay was very young then. He hadn't started a band of any size.
Was Moten -- was Basie one of the piano players with the Moten band then?
Right, right. Yes, Basie was there and all the big bands were there, you know.
But you guys took it?
We captivated the house. There was nothing there but us.
